article_title: Google Open-Sources HEIR, a Compiler Toolchain for Running AI Models on Fully Homomorphic Encrypted Data
summary: Well-sourced and substantively accurate across all 4 sources, but one quote reworks the source's phrasing while presented as verbatim.

findings.message: The article quotes the demos repository as saying the project "has evolved from its origins as a C++ transpiler five years ago into two new open-source libraries." The repository's actual text is: "What started with a C++ transpiler 5 years ago, morphed into two new Open Source libraries." The meaning is preserved but the wording inside the quote marks is reworded, not verbatim.

## Overview

Google is showcasing HEIR, an open-source compiler toolchain that converts pre-trained AI models into versions that can run inference directly on encrypted data, according to a [Google security blog post](https://blog.google/security/how-google-is-making-private-ai-practical-with-homomorphic-encryption/) published August 14, 2026, and written by staff software engineer Jeremy Kun. editor_notes.content_quality: Thorough, well-organized News piece covering a technical announcement across four demos, hardware and research partnerships, and the underlying cryptographic scheme support table. Correctly discloses in 'What We Don't Know' that Google withheld specific latency figures and publication names.
editor_notes.source_verification: Read all 4 snapshots directly. Google's blog post (source-0) confirms nearly every quote and specific verbatim: the 'Private Computing Toolkit' framing, the homomorphic-encryption description, the usability-gap framing, all four demo descriptions with their named partners (Belfort Labs/LG/NYU; Niobium/hardshell.ai; Niobium for Kitsune; Belfort Labs for the hotword detector), the hardware-accelerator partner list, the research-collaboration university list, the four-publications claim, and the private-information-retrieval comparison quote. GitHub's heir repo (source-1) confirms the MLIR-toolchain description, Apache-2.0 license, and the BGV/BFV/CKKS/CGGI backend-support table verbatim. heir.dev (source-3) confirms the audience-description quote and the Python/Torch front-end quote verbatim. Only source-2 (the demos repo) has an issue: the 'evolved from its origins...five years ago' quote reworks the source's actual wording ('What started with a C++ transpiler 5 years ago, morphed into...') while presented as verbatim (see finding). The Jaxite description and 'Make it easy, Make it fast, Make it scale' quote from the same source both check out verbatim.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: All specifics (partner names, backend support matrix, research collaborations, publication count) verify against their cited sources. The one quote-fidelity issue preserves the underlying fact (HEIR's five-year history from a C++ transpiler) while paraphrasing the wording.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral; the Analysis section is clearly framed as analysis and flags the latency-data gap as the key open question rather than taking Google's framing at face value.
editor_notes.originality: Not a duplicate of existing archive content -- no prior HEIR coverage. Note: PR #2211, from the same write-article batch, covers the same underlying August 14 Google blog post with an identical source set, framed around the four demo applications specifically. That framing is fully covered within this article's own body (all four demos are described with their partners), so #2211 does not represent a distinct story; it should be reviewed against this one for rejection as a duplicate once this merges.
concerns: One quote ('evolved from its origins as a C++ transpiler five years ago...') reworks the source's actual phrasing while presented as verbatim -- see the filed corrections record.
recommendations: Added heir.dev to config/source_allowlist.txt -- the HEIR project's own official site (a Google open source project), a legitimate first-party source.
editor_notes.overall_assessment: Approve with corrections. The article is accurate and thoroughly sourced; the single quote-fidelity issue is isolated to a subordinate historical claim and is honestly covered by a public corrections note.
